target_customer: Finance teams at B2B SaaS and enterprise companies: CFOs, controllers, AR managers
problem: Finance teams forecast and collect cash with spreadsheets and manual follow-up, which delays payment and hides shortfalls.
product_category: Accounts receivable and cash flow software

founders.name: Carlos Vega
founders.background_notes: A Snowflake blog bio says he had a decade of finance experience; employers not confirmed.

founders.name: Fabio Fleitas
founders.age_source: Snowflake blog author bio says he co-founded Tesorio at age 20 after meeting Vega at the University of Pennsylvania
founders.background_notes: Same bio says he grew up in Albuquerque.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs integrations with many ERP and billing systems and forecasting models; standard B2B data engineering with some hard parts for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration into ERP and collections workflows creates switching costs, though ERP vendors and large finance suites could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition found. TechCrunch (2019) says other tools handle parts of the workflow; the company remains independent.

market_need_then: The Series A article says finance teams relied on disparate spreadsheets for forecasts. Evidence dated at the 2015 batch was not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses tesorio.com; purchase history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Finance-professional; agent-based product language in 2026 site

branding.community_and_virality: Rated 4.7 of 5 on G2 across 238 reviews per its own site; Madrona IA40 spotlight.

brand_strength.rationale: Customer logos and G2 ratings show product reputation, but no sourced press about the brand itself; a search on the name returns unrelated Tesoro brands.

outcome_analysis: Tesorio went through YC Summer 2015 and started with collections automation before adding cash application and forecasting. It raised a 10 million dollar Series A led by Madrona in August 2019 and a 17 million dollar Series B in July 2022, and lists customers such as Veeva, GitLab and UiPath. It is independent and private, with a founder-led sales motion and no layoff or exit found.
notes: Seed amount and date not found; TechCrunch lists the seed investors as existing investors and three CFO angels, and Tesorio's blog says First Round led the seed. A 6.9M seed figure from Employbl is Diffbot-sourced and unverified. Total after Series B is reported as 37.6M by coverage but 17M plus 17M equals 34M, so a gap of about 3.6M may be an earlier or unlisted round. YC says founded 2013; the company says in business since 2015. Competitors: none named in the 2019 article and no 2015 sources found. No Series C found.
